subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Radar for All Weather
description: A 60-second lesson on Radar for All Weather.

hook.text: Cameras and lidar can be blinded by fog, rain, and snow—radar cuts right through them.

buildup.text: Automotive radar uses radio waves to detect objects, their speed, and their distance.

discovery.text: Radar works day or night, in any weather, making it the most reliable sensor on the car.

twist.text: Its weakness is low resolution—radar sees that something is there but struggles to identify what.

climax.text: New 4D imaging radar adds height data, letting it tell a bridge from a truck for the first time.

punchline.text: Radar sees through anything but can't tell you exactly what it sees.

quiz.question: What is radar's biggest weakness for self-driving cars?

details.summary: Radar sensors use radio waves to detect objects and measure their speed and distance, functioning reliably in rain, fog, snow, and darkness where cameras and lidar can struggle or fail completely.
details.whyItMatters: Radar's all-weather reliability makes it a critical redundant sensor for autonomous vehicles. It ensures that at least one sensing modality works when visual conditions deteriorate.
takeaways: Radar works in rain, fog, snow, and complete darkness
It excels at measuring the speed of moving objects
Radar has lower resolution than cameras or lidar

faq.question: Why did Tesla remove radar from its cars?
faq.answer: Tesla removed forward-facing radar in 2021, claiming its vision-only system performed better. This decision was controversial, as radar provided a reliable backup sensor for measuring distance in poor visibility conditions.

faq.question: What is 4D imaging radar?
faq.answer: Next-generation 4D imaging radar adds height resolution to traditional speed, distance, and angle measurements. This enables radar to create more detailed object profiles, partially bridging the gap with lidar at lower cost.
